jobs.title: Drift Wood #1 · the cafeteria
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 17, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, chin up, unkempt dark hair falling forward, sharp jaw; THE LUNCH LADY — heavyset woman in a white cafeteria smock and hairnet holding a steel ladle, unimpressed posture; GULLY — aged 18, stocky boy with a round face, easy slouch; CHLOE — aged 17, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Wood vs. the lunch line. Truffaut to a lunch lady. Corn. Panel 1: a gaunt teenage boy in an oversized wool overcoat leaning over a cafeteria tray toward a bored lunch lady with a ladle, serving line with a sneeze guard and a heat lamp, fluorescent glare, 1990s high school cafeteria (in this panel: WOOD, THE LUNCH LADY). Wood says "Do you ever consider that this room is the only place in Small Wood where three hundred people voluntarily sit in the same direction?". Panel 2: close two-shot across a cafeteria counter, a lunch lady with a raised ladle giving a flat stare to a gaunt teenage boy in an overcoat, steam rising (in this panel: WOOD, THE LUNCH LADY). Lunch Lady says "Corn or peas.". Panel 3: a teenage boy in a wool overcoat holding a cafeteria tray turns to face the viewer declaiming, the lunch line moving on behind him, heavy black shadows (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "Truffaut said the film of tomorrow will be an act of love. I said corn.". Panel 4: wide shot of a long empty cafeteria table, a teenage boy in an overcoat alone at the near end with a plate of corn, far in the background a boy in a backwards cap drawing on a napkin and a girl with headphones reading, rain on tall windows, lots of empty table (in this panel: WOOD, GULLY, CHLOE). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
